summary: File the imperative “become angry” as detransitive
before: gd-omann-ux ánnaqqa i=qəṣṣa, w k-ubʕət edi áydarbo d-k-ubʕət məqḥár
after: gd-omann-ux ánnaqqa i=qəṣṣa, w k-ubʕət edi áydarbo d-k-ubʕət məqḥár
rationale: The transitive sense is “ärgern” (anger someone), but the imperative məqḥár is addressed to the listener and means “werde so böse, wie du willst”. It illustrates the existing detransitive sense “böse, zornig ... werden”. Retain the imperative form and place it in the corresponding detransitive imperative box.

summary: The dominant corpus pattern is Detransitive qḥir/qḥiro/qḥiri with an experiencer subject, presenting both emotional onset and a sustained state. It need not imply an external angering agent.
Active qoḥarwayli/-lux marks the experiencer with an object suffix. Active qḥare and Detransitive qḥir occur together at 112/315.
m- can identify an anger target; ʕal is not uniformly a target marker: 29/168 means on a companion's account, while 61/340 locates the king on his throne. 59/18 supplies an ʕam stimulus phrase.

qḥiroyo, feminine qhirayto, and qḥiro yo are state predicates filed provisionally under the inherited Nomen Patiens heading. The reader's Part. Pass. labels for the same formation were consolidated here.
qḥənno is recurrent across Lahdo, Prym–Socin and Ritter, making a single printing error unlikely. qḥərwayno supplies a Detransitive Preterit-wa example.
